/itineraryStops/3/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Traditional street-market stalls sell local snacks (Imsil cheese pizza, railroad hotdogs, Winibini candy). Multiple sit-down restaurants serving Korean village-style menus. Hanbok rental free 30-min trial inside the gate.

/itineraryStops/3/whyOnRoute.source_en: The day's biggest heritage block (~2 hours of walking) and the most viscerally late-Joseon stop on the route. 260+ houses representing every region and class, working artisans, equestrian shows, traditional wedding ceremonies, and UNESCO Intangible Heritage Jultagi tightrope walking — all of which dramatize the curated abstraction of Hwaseong's military architecture into visceral living-Joseon experience. **30-min drive each way is offset by 2-hour anchor**. Korean Folk Village is the **definitive sageuk K-drama production set in Greater Seoul** — filming credits include 'Jewel in the Palace / Daejanggeum' (2003-04, peak ratings around 57% in Korea across 54 episodes), 'Sungkyunkwan Scandal' (2010), 'Moonlight Drawn by Clouds' (2016), and many others. For Hallyu-driven travelers, this delivers more authenticity-per-hour than visiting individual filming locations scattered across multiple Korean provinces. A free shuttle bus from Suwon Station Visitor Center (~30 min) or direct Bus 5001-1 from Gangnam Station Exit 5 makes this the most operationally seamless K-drama anchor pair with Hwaseong on a single Seoul-departing day.

/itineraryStops/3/convenience/parking.source_en: Dedicated lot — passenger cars 2,000 KRW, SUVs/trucks 3,000 KRW; tour-coach lot accommodates groups

/itineraryStops/3/description.source_en:
**Korean Folk Village (한국민속촌, Yongin) — Korea's first and largest open-air museum of traditional folk culture**, occupying ~991,735 m² (245 acres / 300,000 pyeong) of natural valley terrain in Yongin city, ~30 minutes drive from Suwon. 

**Over 260 traditional houses and structures reproduced from the late Joseon Dynasty** represent every region of Korea (Seoul, Gyeonggi, Hwanghae, Pyongan, Hamgyong, Gangwon, Chungcheong, Jeolla, Gyeongsang, Jeju) and every social class (commoner farmhouses through yangban scholar-class residences) — a complete sociological tapestry of pre-modern Korea. 

**9 traditional craft workshops** (forge, paper-making, pottery, weaving, etc.) house artisans demonstrating live craft. The village is famous for **daily traditional performances** running on a published schedule: **Nong-ak (farmers' percussion music), Jultagi (tightrope walking — UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Korea, performed with comedic narration), horseback martial arts (mounted acrobatics with sword swings while galloping), and traditional Joseon wedding ceremony reenactments**. 

Performance times typically 10:30/14:00/15:30 — confirm at the entrance. **Hands-on activities**: ferry rides on the village pond, horseback riding, natural fabric dyeing, hanbok rental (free 30-min trial inside the gate), archery range, Confucian School visit. 

A modest amusement-park section with kid-friendly rides is included with combo tickets. **Frequently used as a Joseon-era filming set for K-drama sageuk (historical) productions** — including the iconic **Jewel in the Palace (Daejanggeum, 2003)**, **Sungkyunkwan Scandal (2010)**, **Mr. Sunshine (2018)**, and many others. 

The 'Welcome to Joseon' annual festival is the village's signature spring event; **autumn (last two weeks of October)** is photographically optimal with golden ginkgo and red maple foliage at the yangban two-story house. 

The route's largest single time block (~2 hours of walking) — the most viscerally late-Joseon experience on the day.

/itineraryStops/3/visitBasics/hours.source_en: Mon-Thu 10:00-18:00; Fri-Sun and holidays 10:00-22:00 (winter shorter — Nov-Feb 09:30-17:30)

/itineraryStops/3/visitBasics/admission.source_en: Adult 37,000 / Teen 32,000 / Child 26,000 KRW (Visit Korea official; combo includes amusement-rides section). Folk Village only ~22,000 KRW adult

/itineraryStops/4/smartNotes/tip.source_en: **Library is FREE** — exceptional value attraction. **Free Starfield shuttle from Suwon Station Exit 4** is the easiest access (every 10-15 min). **22-meter bookshelves = Korea's tallest library bookshelves** (mention to guests for impact). **Cherry blossom installation March-April** is the seasonal must-see. Avoid Saturday afternoons (peak crowd density). 1-2 monthly closure days — verify online before visit.

/itineraryStops/4/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Eatopia food hall B1F (30+ restaurants 5,000-40,000 KRW), Toy Kingdom 4F, Aquafield water park B1-2F, T-Joy + CGV + MEGABOX cinema, free WiFi, multilingual customer service, tax-refund counters at major stores.
